newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Observers urge investigation into Armenian vote.
newsitem.headline: Observers urge investigation into Armenian vote.

text.p: An international election observer group has urged an investigation into Armenia's September 22 election, saying irregularities raised "serious questions" about President Levon Ter-Petrosyan's victory.

A nine-page report issued by the U.S.-based International Foundation for Election Systems (IFES), made available to Reuters on Tuesday, said all phases of the electoral process "contained serious compromises or breaks in the law".

It is the second condemnation of the poll by a major group of electoral observers. The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) has also said irregularities were significant enough to call the result into question.

The IFES report, titled "Flawed Elections in Armenia" took a stronger line than the OSCE, saying its monitors witnessed ballot tampering, voter intimidation and the harassment of domestic election monitors.
IFES called for an investigation into the irregularities by the Central Election Commission (CEC).
"In order to invalidate claims of fraud and vote total manipulation, serious and extensive investigations must be undertaken by the CEC as swiftly as possible," it said.
"Failure to do so will ultimately result in substantiating claims of fraud and cast permanent doubt on the transparency of the electoral process," said the report.
Ter-Petrosyan's press secretary Suren Zurabyan responded to the charges by saying the government was not opposed to the country's Constitutional Court hearing challenges to the vote.
"We welcome all demands that talk of checks by the Constitutional Court," he told a gathering of journalists.

The CEC says Ter-Petrosyan won 51.8 percent of the vote compared to 41.3 for former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan. Ter-Petrosyan just cleared a majority hurdle needed to avoid a second round with Manukyan and win a second five-year term.

The 51-year-old former academic sent tanks into the streets of the capital Yerevan and jailed dozens of opposition political figures after some of Manukyan's supporters, saying the vote was rigged, staged a violent protest.
The IFES said that in some instances poll workers intentionally marked ballot papers before giving them to voters in such a way that they would be counted for Ter-Petrosyan or declared invalid.

The report listed abuses in the vote counting process, when it said many ballots or matching vote coupons went missing. It said these irregularities raised "serious questions as to the certainty of the outcome" of the vote.
It said the Central Elections Commission (CEC) had issued "inconsistent" statements regarding vote totals.
It also said Ter-Petrosyan used his control over state television to gain an unfair advantage in election campaigning.
